summary: Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She was a Ph.D. candidate at Lund University (attested 2008), where she was an editor in 2005, and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University, and held posts at EFEO (1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), Collège de France (1987–1992), and Fuzhou University.

Kristóf Szitár is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and Indological studies. He studied at Central European University and the University of Lausanne (Ph.D. 2021–2026), and has held posts at Lausanne, Heidelberg, Yerevan State University, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (MA ~1997–2009) and later served there as a research fellow.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha at Calcutta and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned an M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked for the Chamba State Education Department before serving as a professor and Adhyaksha (1953–1954) at Visva-Bharati University.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).
Kumja Paik Kim is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her doctorate at Stanford University and served as curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum beginning in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and serves as a Research Scholar and Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua and under Franklin Edgerton at Yale (Ph.D. 1955). He held appointments at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and the University of California, Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara at Kyushu University, receiving his degrees there, and held posts as associate professor at Saga University (~1976) and Saga Medical School (~1986).
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1962 to 1969. He subsequently held an academic post at Meiji Gakuin University from approximately 1975 to 2014.

Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga between 1971 and 1976 and served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1993 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He later held academic appointments at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a Japanologist and religious studies scholar who studied law at the University of Tokyo. He held posts in government ministries, at Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, and later taught at Kokugakuin University (~1949–1962) and Keio University.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (~1844–1847). He served on the faculty at Heidelberg University (~1850–1853) and held a professorship at the University of Jena (~1856–1872).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (Ph.D. 1961), and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer (1858–1919) was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1881). He held major academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).

Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Prabal Kumar Sen, Amita Chatterjee, and Shyamapada Misra, she earned her Ph.D. at Jadavpur University (attested 2009) and held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
